course_name_en: INDUSTRIAL AND COMMERCIAL BUILDING SERVICES II
prerequisites: Having completed the subjects of Mathematics and Physics from the Basic Training Module.
Having completed the Technical Thermodynamics subject from the Industrial Branch Common Module.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will learn to condition buildings by understanding the fundamentals of acoustic insulation, hydraulic, gas, and fire suppression systems.
Students will learn to conduct environmental impact studies.
Students will learn to know and understand the importance of occupational safety and health.

syllabus_topics: Notions of acoustics: Waves, properties and types, Physical characterization of sound, Acoustic levels, Perception of sound: loudness, Instrumentation and measurement, Noise, Sound propagation.

Architectural acoustics, Noise propagation in buildings, Acoustic conditioning, Acoustic insulation, Parameters for measuring insulation, Limit values for acoustic insulation, Acoustic insulation exercises.
Legislation, DB HR, Breakdown of DB HR.
The compressed air system. Compressed air. Fundamentals.
Compressors. Types. Selection. Air consumption.
Dry compressed air. Cooler and dryers.
Compressed air tank.
Distribution network.
Introduction (pressure loss, series and parallel coupling, classification of hydraulic pumps).
Water supply to the city.
Water supply in buildings (DB HS 4).
Water drainage (DB HS 5).
Natural Gas. Introduction. Units, Definitions. General notions. Current regulations. Pipelines, Regulation and metering stations. Basic schemes. Calculation of pressure losses, Renourd formulas.
LPG (Propane, Butane) and Diesel Fuels. Introduction. Units and definitions. Current regulations. Pipelines. Tanks.
Applications. Connections. Indoor installations. Consumption appliances. Boilers. Tanks.

Fire protection systems in non-industrial buildings. Current regulations. Study of sectorization. Internal and external propagation. Evacuation of occupants. Active and passive protection provisions. Fire resistance of the structure. Firefighter access.

Fire protection systems in industrial buildings. Current regulations. Study of sectorization. Protection systems for industrial buildings. Fire resistance of the industrial building structure. Structural protection systems.
Environmental Impact Assessment. Introduction. Definitions. National and Autonomous Community legal regulations.
Methodologies applicable to environmental impact study. Typology of impacts. Proposed methodology.
Definitions. Legal regulations. Involved agents.
Occupational Safety and Health Studies. Safety and Health Plans.

assessment_methods.method: Group practical case (including memory, oral/written defense, participation/attendance)

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, students must achieve a score of 5 or higher in the practical case (NCP) and 5 or higher in the final exam (NEF). The final grade (C) is calculated as (NCP + NEF) / 2 and must be 5 or higher to pass. If any condition is not met, the final grade will be the arithmetic mean if it is less than 4.50, and 4.50 if it exceeds this value. The practical case is not recoverable in the ordinary call but is recoverable individually in the extraordinary call. The final exam is recoverable in the extraordinary call. For global evaluation, the final grade (C) is calculated as 0.5 * (Final Exam + Practical Exercise) and must be 5 or higher.
